name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')
principle: An intermediary HTTP agent parses malformed or ambiguous HTTP messages differently from the final client or server. Duplicate Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length conflicts, or incompatible HTTP versions can desynchronize message boundaries and let hidden requests or responses bypass the intermediary.
detection_signals: custom HTTP parser using read()/recv()/readLine() and manual header splitting before proxying
duplicate header handling via map overwrite, e.g. headers.put(name,value), for Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding
code accepts both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding on the same HTTP/1.1 message
code uses first or last Content-Length when multiple Content-Length headers are present
backend connection reuse or HTTP keep-alive/pipelining while forwarding unnormalized request bytes
Java code uses request.getContentLength() without checking request.getHeaders("Content-Length") count
negative_signals: rejects request when more than one Content-Length header is present
rejects request when both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length are present
normalizes/dechunks request body and forwards one canonical Content-Length only
uses a strict RFC-compliant HTTP parser in proxy and origin with identical configuration
closes client/backend connection after each request instead of reusing ambiguous streams
marks proxy-cacheable responses non-cacheable for affected paths
false_defense_traps: TLS/SSL alone does not fix parser disagreement between TLS terminator, proxy, and origin
a WAF in front is bypassable if it parses HTTP differently from the backend
choosing first or last duplicate Content-Length is unsafe instead of rejecting
stripping only exact-case header names misses lowercase or obs-fold variants
disabling cache reduces cache poisoning but not access-control bypass or request smuggling
verification_focus: Does every intermediary and backend reject or canonicalize ambiguous HTTP message lengths before forwarding on a persistent connection?

consequence_chains.trigger: proxy and origin disagree on duplicate Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding plus Content-Length
consequence_chains.consequence: hidden request/response bypasses protection, poisons cache, or reaches unauthorized backend endpoint

patch_principle: Use one strict HTTP parser or matching parser configurations across proxy, firewall, cache, and origin.
Reject duplicate Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length conflicts before forwarding.
Normalize/dechunk messages and forward a single canonical framing header.
Disable backend connection reuse or close the session after each request when strict normalization is not guaranteed.
Make sensitive responses non-cacheable to limit cache poisoning impact.

minimal_examples.vuln: int len = request.getContentLength(); // no check for duplicate Content-Length before proxying
